Aim and objectives

Aim. To explain the structure and physiology of neurones, synapses, receptors and glia for MRCPsych Paper A.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Name the main neurone types and describe the six layers of the neocortex.
  2. Explain the resting membrane potential, action potential generation and saltatory conduction.
  3. Describe synaptic transmission and long-term potentiation through NMDA and AMPA receptors.
  4. Outline computational models of neurones and circuits, such as the Hodgkin-Huxley model and neural networks.
  5. Describe the functions of astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia and Schwann cells.
  6. Answer the chapter's 91 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
